                    ### Question
                    A 49-year-old man is diagnosed with hypertension. He has asthma. The creatinine and potassium levels are both slightly elevated. Which of the following anti-hypertensive drugs would be appropriate in his case?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Amlodipine
opb. Propranolol
opc. Enalapril
opd. Hydrochlorothiazide (HCT)
ope. Spironolactone

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case, the patient has hypertension, asthma, and elevated creatinine and potassium levels. Amlodipine, a calcium channel blocker, is appropriate as it does not adversely affect renal function and is safe for patients with asthma. Propranolol is contraindicated due to its potential to exacerbate asthma symptoms. Enalapril, an ACE inhibitor, is not suitable as it can worsen renal function, especially in the presence of elevated creatinine. Hydrochlorothiazide may cause electrolyte imbalances and is not ideal due to the elevated potassium levels. Spironolactone, a potassium-sparing diuretic, is also inappropriate as it can further elevate potassium levels. Therefore, the best choice is Amlodipine.
